question_text: Graphite is an electric conductor whereas diamond is not. Why?

steps.label: Why graphite conducts
lines: In graphite each carbon atom is sp²
hybridised and forms only three sigma

A moving electron is a current, so
steps.why: The comparison rests on one number: how many of carbon's four valence electrons are used in bonds. In graphite three are used and one is left over, and that spare electron is what carries the current.
common_mistakes: Giving the sliding layers as the reason for conduction. The layers explain why graphite is a lubricant, not why it conducts.
Writing that graphite conducts because it is a metal. Graphite is a non-metal; the delocalised electrons come from its own structure.
steps.memory_tip: Three bonds in graphite leave one electron free to move.
steps.margin_note: The question has two halves. This half is graphite, so answer it in full before starting on diamond.

steps.label: Why diamond does not
lines: In diamond each carbon atom is sp³
hybridised and forms four sigma bonds
All four valence electrons are used up
in those bonds, so there is no free or
Diamond is therefore a bad conductor of

lines.text: Free electron in graphite, none in diamond

steps.why: Diamond is the comparison that proves the point. Its bonds are made of exactly the same element and are just as covalent, and the one thing it lacks is a spare electron — which shows that the spare electron, not the element, is what does the conducting.
common_mistakes: Saying diamond does not conduct because its bonds are strong. Bond strength is not the reason; the reason is that no electron is left over.
Writing that diamond conducts electricity weakly. It is a bad conductor of electricity, because it has no free electrons.
steps.memory_tip: Four bonds in diamond use up all four electrons, so none is left.
steps.margin_note: Say plainly that diamond has no free electron; that sentence is the second half of the answer.

insider_note: The question has two halves, so a complete answer explains graphite's delocalised fourth electron and then says diamond uses all four of its valence electrons in bonds and has none left over.
